summary: Entera Bio reported Q1 2020 financial results with a net loss of $2.9 million and cash of $13.3 million, expecting to fund operations into Q2 2021. The company plans to study higher doses within current 2020 spend and expects six-month BMD data in Q3 2020, with Phase 3 targeted for late 2021 or 2022. COVID-19 caused moderate enrollment delays, but operations are resuming.

summary: For Q2 FY2020, Salarius Pharmaceuticals reported a net loss of $1.8 million ($0.13 per share), wider than the prior-year loss of $0.9 million ($0.30 per share) due to higher R&D and G&A costs. Cash stood at $7.2 million at quarter-end, supplemented by a $6.2 million offering in August and up to $9.1 million in grant funding, extending runway to late 2021. Early seclidemstat data show dose-proportional plasma levels and a reduction in target lesions in one patient, though RECIST classified the patient as progressive disease. The company plans to expand its Ewing sarcoma trial to include Ewing-related sarcomas, increasing expansion cohort from 20 to 50 patients, with early data expected in the second half of 2021.

summary: Entera Bio reported interim six-month data from the Phase 2 trial of EB613, showing a placebo-adjusted 2.15% increase in lumbar spine BMD at the 1.5 mg dose (p=0.08) and a significant dose-dependent trend across all doses. The company added a higher 2.5 mg dose group and discontinued lower doses, aiming to start a Phase 3 trial in late 2021 or 2022. H1 2020 revenue was $94,000 from the Amgen collaboration, with total operating expenses of $6.4 million and cash sufficient into Q2 2021. Enrollment was back on track with 131 subjects, and no serious drug-related adverse events were reported.

summary: Entera Bio completed enrollment of its Phase 2 EB613 trial with 161 patients despite COVID-19. The company expects final biomarker data including the new 2.5 mg dose in Q1 2021 and final BMD data in Q2 2021. Cash of $7.1 million at September 30, 2020 is expected to fund operations into Q2 2021, with an anticipated 2020 operating loss of approximately $11 million.

Management expects readouts around end of Q4 2021 or Q1 2022 and plans multiple new trials by mid-2021.

positive_highlights: Wavelo revenue up 174% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $4.2 million, its strongest quarter since launch

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 13% year-over-year, partly due to currency effects.
Q4 2023 expected to be negatively impacted by the Israel-Hamas war.
Slow-moving inventory discounts reduced average note price to $4.35 per gram.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 22% from 20% year-over-year.

Operating expenses reduced by 34% year-over-year.
summary: In Q3 2023, IM Cannabis reported revenues of $12.4 million, down 13% from $14.2 million in Q3 2022, with 6.4% of the decline attributed to unfavorable currency effects. Operating expenses fell 34% year-over-year, but the company faced headwinds from slow-moving inventory discounts, a delivery transition, and the onset of the Israel-Hamas war, which is expected to negatively impact Q4. Management remains focused on sustainable profitability and anticipates regulatory changes in Germany and Israel, but notes delays due to the war.

Pivotal trial costs estimated at $18M (AML) with no guarantee of external funding

summary: Moleculin reported preliminary Phase 2 data for Annamycin in AML and STS, showing a 38% complete response rate in heavily pre-treated AML patients and a 78% response rate with 56% 3-month PFS in STS at the optimal dose. Management is planning end-of-Phase 2 meetings with FDA/EMA and expects to start pivotal trials in 2024, with potential external funding for the STS pivotal trial.

summary: Moleculin Biotech reported clinical data from its Annamycin program in relapsed/refractory AML, with a 60% CRc rate (50% CR, 10% CRi) in second-line patients from the MB-106 trial. Management also mentioned interest from European sarcoma experts for an externally funded trial, while the company ended 2023 with $24 million in cash, sufficient into Q4 2024. The tone is confident, emphasizing superior efficacy versus approved targeted therapies and a clear regulatory pathway.

Management remains confident in market fundamentals, citing low order books and supportive demand, and highlighted a strong cash balance of $35.6 million with no bank debt.

summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue fell to $19.4M from $20.6M YoY, with strong EV charging growth (+40% to $4.7M) and maintenance rebound, but LED lighting was hit by customer project delays. Management revised FY2025 revenue growth outlook to ~10% from 10-15%, citing delays shifting revenue to the second half. They expect positive adjusted EBITDA in the second half and neutral for the full year. New contracts announced include a $25M LED supply deal and a $10M+ multi-year project.

Net revenue up 29% to $81.1 million, with record medical cannabis revenue up 41% YoY
International medical cannabis revenue up 93%, now 57% of global medical revenue
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported strong Q2 FY2025 results with net revenue up 29% to $81.1 million, record medical cannabis revenue of $61.3 million (up 41% YoY), and record adjusted EBITDA of $10.1 million (up 210% YoY). International medical revenue surged 93%, now 57% of global medical revenue, and the company guided to positive free cash flow in Q3. Management expressed confidence in continued profitable growth driven by international expansion, particularly in Germany and Australia.

Added compounded semaglutide, driving the single highest day for clinic sign-ups in 2024
B2B channel sees positive Q4 note season with newly contracted partnerships
summary: WW International reported Q3 2024 results that were broadly on track with expectations, but acknowledged significant work ahead to revert to growth. Clinic member retention improved to 7.5 months from 6.5 months, and adding compounded semaglutide drove a record day for clinic sign-ups, though overall impact on 2024 is expected to be immaterial. Management announced a $100 million cost action plan with full run-rate savings by end of 2025, while noting elevated customer acquisition costs and ongoing medication shortages. They are not guiding 2025 yet, but expressed optimism about long-term opportunities in clinical and B2B segments.

summary: Kaltura's Q3 2024 revenue of $44.3M (+2% YoY) and subscription revenue of $42.1M (+3% YoY) both exceeded guidance. Adjusted EBITDA of $2.4M marked a fifth consecutive profitable quarter, and operating cash flow hit a record $10.7M. Full-year guidance was raised again, with expectations of positive annual cash flow from operations for the first time since 2020.

summary: Noodles & Company reported Q3 2024 results impacted by a difficult consumer environment, elevated competitive discounting, and a sudden drop in third-party delivery sales. They guided full-year revenue to $487-495 million with negative comps of 3% to -1.5%, and restaurant contribution margin between 12.7% and 13.3%. The company rolled out three new menu items in October, which improved traffic from roughly -6% to -0.8% quarter-to-date in Q4, and they reduced capex to under $15M for 2025 expecting free cash flow positive. They are testing new menu markups in delivery to regain traffic and announced a credit facility amendment for flexibility.

First oral TPOXX sale in Africa, expanding international reach
summary: SIGA reported Q3 2024 product revenue of $9 million, with nine-month product revenue of $53 million, outpacing the prior year. The company secured $122 million in procurement orders during the quarter, ending with $146 million in outstanding orders, positioning for strong Q4 and 2025 revenue. Net income for Q3 was $1 million ($0.02 per diluted share), and cash stood at $99 million with no debt. Management expects a new Strategic National Stockpile (SNS) contract in 2025, targeting a 5-10 year agreement with initial order, and highlighted ongoing mpox studies and a new monoclonal antibody license from Vanderbilt University.

summary: MBIA reported a net loss of $56 million for Q3 2024, improved from a $185 million loss in Q3 2023, with adjusted net loss nearly breakeven. The improvement was driven by lower loss and loss adjustment expenses at National related to PREPA, though uncertainty around the PREPA bankruptcy persists with mediation extended to January 2025. National's insured portfolio declined to $26 billion, and the company holds $326 million unencumbered cash at the holding company. The company remains cautious on watching the company due to PREPA uncertainty but is open to considering seller structures with back-end payments.

summary: Hagerty reported Q3 2024 total revenue of $323 million, up 17% year-over-year, with written premiums up 13% and retention improving to 89%. The quarter included $25 million of catastrophe losses from Hurricane Helene, which pressured operating income to $10 million and adjusted EBITDA to $24 million, down from prior year. For the full year, management raised revenue guidance to $1.18 billion (18-19% growth) and maintained underlying profit outlook, while adjusting net income to $65-74 million and adjusted EBITDA to $110-120 million to reflect $30 million of combined Helene and Milton losses. Management highlighted strong cost discipline, record new member additions, and growth initiatives like State Farm rollout and Enthusiast Plus launch in 2025.

summary: AlTi reported Q3 2024 revenues of $53.3 million, up 11% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $9.6 million, a $12.6 million improvement versus the prior year. Core Wealth & Capital Solutions segment revenue increased 17% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA grew 62% with margin expanding from 19% to 26%. The company took a $116.1 million non-cash impairment charge, largely due to goodwill write-downs in real estate and event-driven strategy intangibles, and is reviewing strategic options for its real estate businesses with a decision expected by year-end. Management is confident, highlighting strong organic growth, the Allianz partnership, and continued cost discipline.

The company cited distributor inventory normalization and improved lead times as temporary revenue drags, and noted distributor inventories have normalized. Management reaffirmed long-term targets of 40% gross margin and 20%+ EBITDA margin, while highlighting strong D2C growth, new product revenue up 25%, and a 133% improvement in revenue per new product launch.

summary: In Q3 FY2024, Tigo Energy reported revenue of $14.2 million, down 16.8% YoY but up 12.1% sequentially. Gross margin fell to 12.5% due to a $3.4 million battery inventory charge; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $8.3 million. Management raised market share gains and strong growth in newer regions like Czech Republic and Australia, but noted sluggishness in Germany, Italy, and Netherlands. Q4 guidance is $14-17 million revenue and $6.5-8.5 million adjusted EBITDA loss, with potential additional inventory charges. EBITDA breakeven is expected in 2025, likely H2.

summary: NCDL reported Q3 2024 net investment income of $0.58 per share, fully covering its regular and special dividends of $0.45 and $0.10 per share, with total GAAP net income of $0.67 per share including $0.09 of net realized and unrealized gains. Net asset value rose to $18.15 per share from $18.03, and the company originated $226 million of new investments, with no new non-accruals and non-accruals at roughly 1.5% of fair value. Management expressed optimism for 2025, citing moderate spread compression, expected M&A pickup, and a large repurchase program with $14 million used of a $100 million authorization.

Phase III HCV program expected to start early next year
summary: Atea reported Q3 2024 results with cash of $482.8 million, down from $492.8 million at the start of Q4, and expects cash runway into 2027. The key event was the failure of the SUNRISE-3 COVID-19 trial, which did not meet expectations due to milder disease and no hospitalizations. The company is pivoting to its HCV program, with Phase II top-line results expected in early December and Phase III planned for early 2025. R&D expenses decreased mainly due to lower COVID-19 spending.

summary: Consolidated Q3 revenue grew 6.1% YoY to $92.3M, gross profit up 32.4% to $22.2M, and adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $8.7M from $4.5M, driven by Domains and Ting improvements. Domains revenue rose 5.9% to $64.7M with EBITDA up 5.6% to $11.5M, while Wavelo revenue declined 9% to $10.1M and EBITDA fell 18.5% to $3.4M. Ting revenue grew 19% to $15.3M, EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.1M from $12.2M, and net additions were 1,400. Management reduced Ting workforce by 40% to cut ~$22M in cash costs, stopped expansion, and expects Ting to be near adjusted EBITDA breakeven in 2025. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA year-to-date exceeded $22M, on track to approximately double from 2023's $15.5M.

summary: Profound Medical reported Q3 2024 revenue of $2.83 million, up 64% YoY, with recurring revenue of $2.65 million and $179k capital equipment. Net loss widened to $9.4 million ($0.38/share) from $5.6 million, with cash at $27.1 million. CMS final rule set TULSA reimbursement at urology APC Level 7, with average facility payment of $12,992 in hospitals and $10,728 in ASCs, both above other prostate procedures. Management reaffirmed FY2024 revenue guidance of $11-12 million and highlighted increasing CAPTAIN trial recruitment including Cleveland Clinic, with data expected by AUA 2025.

summary: Nuwellis reported Q3 2024 revenue of $2.4 million, down 2% year-over-year but up 8% sequentially, with a 28% surge in pediatric category. Gross margin improved to 70% from 57.3%, while operating loss narrowed to $1.5 million from $3.2 million, though net income was driven by a $3.9 million warrant revaluation benefit. The company highlighted a significant CMS reimbursement increase effective January 1, 2025, raising the facility fee from $413 to $1,639 per day (297% increase), which management expects to accelerate growth. Cash balance was $1.9 million at quarter end, with additional $5.1 million raised from warrant exercises after quarter end.

positive_highlights: Phase 2 CR rate of 50% in second-line AML patients, more than double existing therapies
Median durability of responses now 8 months and still climbing; 78% MRD-negative
FDA-specified adaptive design and early unblinding reduce approval risk
summary: Moleculin reported Q3 2024 with $9.4 million cash on hand, sufficient to fund operations into Q1 2025. The company highlighted its Phase 2 data for Annamycin in AML, including 50% complete remission in second-line patients, median durability of 8 months, and 78% MRD-negative responses. The Phase 3 MIRACLE trial is underway with adaptive design, and management emphasized de-risking via early unblinding and the possibility of accelerated approval if interim results are strong. Financial guidance was not provided; cash runway is short.

The company lowered its full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $56-58 million (11-15% growth) from prior expectations of a sharper second-half recovery. CFO noted a 5% organic revenue decline excluding RedWave. Management is implementing structural changes including an 11% workforce reduction and manufacturing consolidation to save ~$4.2 million and ~$2.4 million annually respectively.

Gross deployment was $73 million, with net realizations of $20 million, and the company completed additional First Eagle rotation. Management expressed confidence in portfolio credit and is constructive on 2025 activity due to rate cuts and election optimism, but noted higher non-recurring income and PIK this quarter.

summary: NeuroPace reported Q3 2024 revenue of $21.1 million, up 28% year-over-year, driven primarily by RNS System sales which grew 36% excluding NAUTILUS study cases. Gross margin was 73.2%, within the 72-74% target. Net loss narrowed to $5.5 million from $7.3 million, and cash burn reduced to $1.8 million, with cash ending at $56.8 million. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $78-$80 million, implying 19-22% growth. Operational highlights include record active prescribers, Project CARE momentum, and progress on NAUTILUS with one-year follow-up expected in Q1 2025.

summary: PublicSquare reported Q3 FY2024 net revenue of $6.5 million, up 222% year-over-year, with Fintech contributing $3.2 million from watch now, pay later only, as payments revenue starts in Q4. Gross margin expanded to 64% from 27%, driven by high-margin credit products. Management signed contracts potentially exceeding $1 billion in annualized GMV for its payments platform, ahead of schedule, and activated its first enterprise merchant expected to process over $100 million annually. The company reduced workforce by over 35% to save an estimated $11 million annually, aiming for segment and overall cash flow positivity in 2025.

summary: Broadwind reported Q3 2024 revenue of $35.9 million, down 35% year-over-year due to lower wind tower demand, but delivered near double-digit EBITDA margin (9.5%) and its seventh consecutive profitable quarter. Orders increased 45% year-over-year, with industrial orders up 52% and gearing up 46%, though gearing orders remain below desired levels. Management introduced Q4 revenue guidance of $31-$33 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1-$1.5 million, while expecting 2025 wind volumes to be similar to 2024 with an uptick in activity later in the year.

Adjusted EBITDA improved to $800,000 from $300,000 in the prior year, with the Surgical segment generating positive EBITDA. The company invested $5 million in ChemoMouthpiece LLC for a 6.6% stake and exclusive distribution through its InfuSystem JV, while Tissue Health Plus remains on track for a mid-2025 commercial launch.

summary: Xos reported Q3 2024 revenue of $15.8 million, up 1.6% sequentially, with GAAP gross margin of 18.1% (15% excluding clean energy credits), marking the fifth consecutive quarter of positive margins. Unit deliveries were 94 units, up 4.4% sequentially, and the company achieved low-volume series production of its hub product, shipping nearly 12 hubs. Non-GAAP operating loss improved to $6.6 million from $9.7 million in Q2, and free cash flow improved to negative $11.7 million from negative $26.1 million. However, the company lowered its full-year 2024 revenue and unit delivery guidance, now expecting revenue of $54.1-$67.6 million and deliveries of 320-400 units, while narrowing non-GAAP operating loss to $33.7-$42.2 million, citing infrastructure and customer delays. Cash stood at $9.2 million, and inventory increased to $42.4 million, with over $25 million in incentive receivables backlog.

The company secured a seven-figure multi-year contract with a North American operator, with revenue recognition beginning in 2025, and raised its full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $59-62 million from prior levels, expecting a fifth consecutive year of revenue growth and increased profitability. Management expressed confidence in the pipeline, citing strong demand for 5G assurance and AI capabilities, and announced a new CEO starting December 1.

Gross margin contracted to 46% from 52.3%, but G&A dropped $1.3M and net loss improved to $3.5M from $5.4M. Management highlighted a new VAYNERCOMMERCE partnership that drove a 34% increase in daily digital revenues during a 17-day period, and expects a $4.5M earnings benefit in 2025 from non-cash expense amortization ending and interest expense declining, plus a wholesale price increase at Sundry adding over $500K annually. The company is pivoting from debt repayment to growth initiatives.

Nu.Q Vet test revenue grew 307% in the quarter and 100% YTD, with over 110,000 tests sold in the first nine months. The company lowered outsourced linehaul miles to 8.8% of total miles, a record low, and highlighted ongoing technology and AI investments aimed at further productivity gains. Management expressed confidence in continued above-market yield growth and margin expansion, while noting the uncertain macro environment and expected moderation in CapEx.

The company guided Q2 sales to $149-157 million and adjusted EBITDA to $10-13 million, citing tariff uncertainty, lower residential demand, and softer energy markets. Management expressed cautious optimism around operational improvements but noted significant external headwinds.

Guidance was narrowed with the floor raised to 48,000 Boe/d, and management highlighted significant drilling efficiencies (spud-to-spud down to 11 days) and expects further cost savings from simul-frac operations. North America gross margin pressured by input costs and inefficiencies; 540 bps decline
Europe/APAC combined revenue down 2.7% with flat volumes, EU tariffs and destocking
positive_highlights: Eighth consecutive quarter of volume growth, with 5.2% volume growth overall
Automation revenue increased 34% with robust backlog; full year $40-$45 million expected
Potential multiyear North America deal worth over $100 million could consume Shelton capacity
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 3.8% on a constant currency basis, with North America up 12.2% and volumes up 14.8%, but adjusted EBITDA declined 18% due to input cost, mix, and inefficiencies. The company is executing $8 million in cost-out actions and expects margin and EBITDA improvement in H2, with automation revenue guided to $40-$45 million. A potential multiyear North America automation deal worth over $100 million was highlighted, but no formal guidance was raised.

negative_highlights: Arcadia sales down 11% YoY on weak high-end residential demand
NobelClad backlog fell to $37 million from $41 million due to tariff-driven lost business
Third-quarter guidance implies sales down $5-13 million sequentially and EBITDA down $1.5-5.5 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million exceeded the $10-13 million guidance range
Total debt reduced 17% sequentially to $59 million
DynaEnergetics adjusted EBITDA margin rose 210 bps sequentially and 190 bps YoY to 13.4%
summary: DMC Global reported Q2 FY2025 consolidated sales of $155.5 million and adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $13.5 million, exceeding the guidance range of $10 million to $13 million. Arcadia sales declined 11% YoY, DynaEnergetics declined 12%, while NobelClad grew 6% but saw backlog fall to $37 million from $41 million. The company cut total debt by 17% to $59 million. Third-quarter guidance is soft at $142-150 million sales and $8-12 million EBITDA due to tariff uncertainty, high interest rates, and weak energy activity.

negative_highlights: Connected machines revenue decreased 10% due to fewer units sold
Engagement erosion persists, though moderating: 90-day engaged users down 2% versus down 3% a year ago
Subscriber growth may be flat to declining in Q3 due to natural attrition, and Q2 benefited from pull-forward of accessories demand
positive_highlights: Operating income grew 14% and EPS grew 22% YoY
Total gross margin expanded to 59% from 53.5%, with Products gross margin up to 32.4% from 23.3%
Paid subscribers grew 7% YoY to over 3 million, with new user engagement (cuts in first 30 days) improving
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 2% to $172.1M, with operating income up 14% and EPS up 22%. Platform revenue grew 4% to $80.7M, and Products grew 1% to $91.4M, with connected machines down 10% but accessories and materials up 12% due to tariff-driven pull-forward of shipments. Paid subscribers reached 3+ million, up 7% YoY, while ARPU rose 2% to $53.84. Gross margin expanded significantly, particularly in Products, up to 32.4% from 23.3%. Management cited moderation in engagement erosion but remains cautious on tariff impacts and subscriber seasonality, guiding to potential flat/declining subscriber count in Q3.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 49% from 54% due to amortization and warranty costs
Adjusted gross margin down 220 basis points to 56% driven by higher warranty costs
Operating expenses increased to $21.5 million from $14.7 million due to noncash charges
positive_highlights: Revenue up 14% YoY to $13 million, above internal expectations
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 45% YoY and 15% QoQ
Record XplorIR units shipped in Q2, with 164 devices placed
summary: 908 Devices reported Q2 2025 revenue of $13 million, up 14% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA loss improving 45% year-over-year and 15% sequentially. The company highlighted record XplorIR placements and strong legislative tailwinds, while maintaining its goal of adjusted EBITDA positive by Q4 2025. They launched VipIR, acquired KAF Manufacturing, and completed facility consolidations to reduce costs.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis revenue fell to $7.9 million from $11.5 million due to strategic shift
Plant propagation adjusted gross margin dropped to 6% from 18% due to nonrecurring quality issue
Q2 free cash flow expected to be impacted by significant cash outflows
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 209% to $10.8 million from $3.5 million
International revenue grew 85% and adjusted gross margin improved 1,000 bps to 52%
Positive free cash flow of $9.2 million; cash rose to $186 million with no cannabis debt
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported strong Q1 FY2026 results with net revenue up 17% to $98 million, global medical cannabis revenue up 37%, and international revenue up 85%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 1,000 basis points to 52%, and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $10.8 million. The company achieved positive free cash flow of $9.2 million and ended with $186 million in cash, with no cannabis debt. Management raised no explicit full-year guidance but issued Q2 guidance for 8-12% global medical cannabis growth and continued positive adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: CHMP referral raises questions on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox
International orders expected to remain lumpy
US government RFP timing uncertain, with negotiation expected to take months
positive_highlights: Product revenues of $79M in Q2, fulfilling $70M of outstanding orders
Received $27M in incremental development funding from US government
Pretax operating income of $46M and net income of $35M, with no debt
summary: Q2 2025 product revenue was $79 million (oral TPOXX $53M, IV TPOXX $26M), fulfilling $70M of prior-year orders, with $26M in remaining IV TPOXX orders targeted for 2026 delivery. Pretax operating income was $46 million for the quarter, net income $35 million, and fully diluted EPS $0.49. The U.S. government committed $27 million in incremental development funding under the BARDA 19C contract ($14M manufacturing, $13M pediatric). The CHMP initiated a referral on tecovirimat efficacy for mpox, while management remains confident in the smallpox indication.

negative_highlights: Revenue essentially flat at $19.6 million vs $19.9 million
EV charging revenue fell to $2.7 million from $3.8 million, citing project timing
EV financing uncertainty and tariff concerns noted
positive_highlights: Gross margin reached 30.1%, highest in about six years
Third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
New $6.5 million Boston Public Schools EV charging expansion win
summary: Orion reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $19.6 million, roughly flat year-over-year, with LED lighting up 1% and maintenance up 21%, offset by a decline in EV charging due to project timing. Gross margin expanded 850 basis points to 30.1%, and net loss narrowed to $1.2 million from $3.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA positive for the third consecutive quarter. CEO stated confidence in achieving FY2026 revenue of about $84 million and positive adjusted EBITDA. Guidance was reiterated, not raised.

negative_highlights: Lift Truck revenues declined 19% year-over-year, with volumes down across all product lines
Q2 bookings fell to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, driven by tariff-related demand deferrals
Q2 adjusted operating profit down to $5 million, with tariff-driven costs of $10 million
positive_highlights: Operating cash flow improved to ~$30 million in Q2, up from prior year and prior quarter
Unused borrowing capacity increased 3% to nearly $260 million
Bolzoni revenue grew sequentially with improved margins from mix shift
summary: In Q2 FY2025, Hyster-Yale reported Lift Truck revenues down 19% year-over-year, with adjusted operating profit falling sharply to $5 million, impacted by $10 million in tariff-driven costs. Bookings declined to $330 million from $590 million in Q1, and backlog fell from $1.9 billion to $1.7 billion. The company maintained its full-year guidance but emphasized heightened economic uncertainty, tariff volatility, and a cyclical demand trough, while planning to increase production in H2 to meet an expected demand uptick.

negative_highlights: Gross originations declined to $48 million from $166 million quarter-over-quarter
Net investment income fell to $0.46 per share from $0.53 due to fee changes
Net asset value declined from $17.96 to $17.92 per share on valuation losses
positive_highlights: Net investment income of $0.46 per share exceeded the quarterly distribution of $0.45
Nonaccruals improved to 0.2% of fair value, down from 0.4%
Pipeline increasing with deal reviews up over 60% from April to June
summary: NCDL reported Q2 2025 net investment income of $0.46 per share, covering its $0.45 dividend, but down from $0.53 in Q1 due to the expiration of an incentive fee waiver and intentional leverage reduction. Gross originations fell to $48 million from $166 million, reflecting a deliberate slowdown, with portfolio fair value down slightly to $2 billion. Credit quality improved with nonaccruals dropping to 0.2% of fair value, and NAV dipped to $17.92 per share. Management sees positive momentum in the second half with a stronger pipeline and completed rotation to core middle market assets.

negative_highlights: Book value per share decreased to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99.
Corporate unencumbered cash fell to $355 million from $380 million at year-end.
PREPA resolution timing remains uncertain; Oversight Board changes add unpredictability.
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss narrowed to $56 million from $254 million year-over-year.
Transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to custodian to improve marketability.
National statutory capital rose to $914 million from $912 million at year-end.
summary: MBIA reported a narrower GAAP net loss of $56 million in Q2 2025 versus $254 million a year ago, primarily due to lower losses on PREPA exposure. Adjusted net loss was $8 million, improved from $138 million last year. Book value per share declined to negative $43.14 from negative $40.99. Management emphasized persistent PREPA uncertainty and noted a newly transferred $374 million of PREPA claims to a custodian to enhance marketability, while still considering the sale process. Guidance is not applicable, but tone is cautious and forward-looking about PREPA resolution.

negative_highlights: M&T revenue declined 14% YoY, the sharpest decline ever
10% workforce reduction announced, with cost savings only starting in Q3
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guided down sequentially due to one-time benefits in Q2
positive_highlights: Subscription and total revenue both above the high end of guidance
Record non-GAAP net profit of $2.5 million and eighth consecutive quarter of adjusted EBITDA profitability
First three AI deals closed, with 100+ qualified AI pipeline opportunities
summary: Kaltura reported Q2 2025 total revenue of $44.5 million, up 1% YoY, and subscription revenue of $42.4 million, up 3% YoY, both above the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.1 million, record non-GAAP net profit of $2.5 million, and cash flow from operations of $2.7 million, with gross margin up to 70% from 66% YoY. EE&T revenue grew 7% YoY, its highest since Q1 2022, while M&T revenue declined 14% YoY, its sharpest ever. The company announced a restructuring that will cut ~10% of workforce, with expected savings of $2.6 million in 2025 and $8.5 million annualized, but reaffirmed full-year guidance and expects strong Q4 with M&T sequential growth.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin down 74 basis points year-over-year
Forward guidance reflects conservative H2 outlook amid economic uncertainty
Safety and Racing division growth tempered by Snell cycle regulatory transition
positive_highlights: Core business revenue grew 3.9% year-over-year, with all divisions positive
Record quarterly free cash flow of $35.7 million, up $11.3 million year-over-year
Tariff mitigation plan working; no meaningful impact to cash flow or margins expected
summary: Holley reported Q2 2025 core revenue growth of 3.9% to $166.7 million, with record quarterly free cash flow of $35.7 million. Gross margin expanded 26 basis points to 41.7%, while adjusted EBITDA margin declined 74 basis points to 21.9%. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2025 guidance, taking a conservative stance on H2 due to macroeconomic uncertainty, though tariff mitigation is on track.

negative_highlights: No revenue or product sales; company is pre-commercialization
Cash balance decreased to $379.7 million from prior periods (interest income lower)
Phase III data not available until 2026

Enrollment in Phase III trials is on track; top-line data expected mid-2026 and end of 2026
Market research: 76% of high U.S. DAA prescribers extremely likely to prescribe regimen
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 2025 progress with its HCV regimen bemnifosbuvir/ruzavir, highlighting 98% SVR12 in the primary efficacy analysis at EASL. Phase III enrollment is on track, with top-line results expected mid-2026 (C-BEYOND) and end of 2026 (C-FORWARD). Cash balance is $379.7 million, with runway through 2027, and the company repurchased 4.6 million shares under a $25 million buyback. Market research shows 76% of high U.S. DAA prescribers extremely likely to prescribe the regimen.

negative_highlights: Residential market flat over past two quarters; outlook depends on macro factors
Noncash tax provision of $206,000 reduced reported EPS
Telco contract timing depends on customer installation pace
positive_highlights: Revenue up 55% YoY to $3.5 million, with hardware up 89% and monitoring up 19%
Gross margin expanded to 75% from 73%; operating income up 267%
Uplisted to NASDAQ; R&D up 17% supporting new product launches
summary: Acorn Energy reported record Q2 FY2025 revenue of $3.5 million, up 55% year-over-year, driven by an 89% increase in hardware sales and 19% growth in monitoring revenue. Gross margin expanded to 75%, operating income rose 267% to $947,000, and fully diluted EPS was $0.28 (excluding noncash taxes, EPS would be $0.36). The company uplisted to NASDAQ, launched next-generation Omni and OmniPro monitors, and reiterated a 20% average annual revenue growth target over the next 3-5 years. Management highlighted a $5.4 million telecom contract with $4.1 million recognized to date, strong cash flow, and a debt-free balance sheet.

negative_highlights: Ting adjusted EBITDA loss of $3.7M in Q2, though improved YoY before noncash lease adjustment.
Corporate net debt high at $190.3M; leverage 3.14x, though declining.
Macro signals mixed; management remains cautious and conservative.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 10% YoY to $98.5M, fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth.
Wavelo delivered best quarter ever: revenue +21% YoY, adjusted EBITDA +37% YoY.
New Radix registry contract to migrate >10M domains, boosting registry to ~17M domains.
summary: Tucows Q2 FY2025 revenue grew 10% YoY to $98.5M, with gross profit up 6% to $22.1M (absorbing a $2.7M noncash lease adjustment at Ting) and adjusted EBITDA up 37% to $12.6M. Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA of $26.2M is slightly ahead of the run-rate for full-year guidance of $47M. Domains and Wavelo outperformed, with Wavelo posting its best quarter (revenue +21% YoY, EBITDA +37%). Ting revenue grew 13% with subscribers up 8%, but remains loss-making; the company signed a landmark senior-living bulk contract and sold nonstrategic assets for over $15M. Guidance maintained.

negative_highlights: Q3 volume guidance below Q2 actuals
Gain on sale margin down to 330bps from 355bps
CEO acknowledges market share has shrunk
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss narrowed from $25M to $16M
Origination volume up 30% sequentially
Direct origination expenses down 7% despite 30% volume increase
summary: Q2 2025 adjusted net loss narrowed to $16M from $25M in Q1 on higher lock volume and lower costs. Pull-through weighted rate lock volume was $6.3B, up 17% sequentially and within guidance; origination volume was $6.7B, up 30% and within guidance. Gain on sale margin was 330bps, down from 355bps and within guidance. Q3 guidance calls for lower volumes and margins, reflecting market volatility and high rates. CEO returned permanently and focuses on regaining market share and profitability.

negative_highlights: Residual noise from bankruptcy process was acute in Q2
Ceased prescribing compounded semaglutide on May 22, expecting subscriber roll-off through August
Competitors remain aggressive in marketing compounded GLP-1s via personalization exemption
positive_highlights: Debt reduced by more than 70%, freeing ~$50M cash annually from lower interest expense
Positive momentum for core branded business on both year-over-year and sequential basis
12-month weight loss of 19.4% compared to next highest competitor at 15.8%
summary: In Q2 FY2025, WeightWatchers completed a strategic reorganization, reducing debt by more than 70% and relisting on NASDAQ. Revenue and subscriber growth were pressured by the bankruptcy process and the May 22 FDA deadline on compounded semaglutide, with a sequential decline expected in Q3 as members transition off compounded medications. Management highlighted positive momentum in the branded medication business, strategic partnerships with Lilly and Novo Nordisk, and long-term growth plans in clinical care, B2B, and women's health, but acknowledged near-term headwinds. Guidance was not explicitly provided; management only reiterated long-term confidence while expecting continued roll-off of compounding members through August.

Three major advertisers have not resumed spending; Q3 guide excludes them
Contribution ex-TAC growth (16%) lagged revenue growth (18%), partly due to deliberate pass-through of AI savings
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 18% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $11.3 million, surpassing guidance midpoint
AI Bidding contribution ex-TAC doubled year-over-year
summary: Viant reported Q2 2025 revenue up 18% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 16% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $11.3 million, surpassing the midpoint of guidance. CTV drove growth, with Household ID spend up 15% YoY, and AI Bidding now automates 85% of ad spend. Q3 guidance implies a slowdown due to a 4-point political headwind and excludes any resumption of delayed advertiser spending, while a $250 million gross spend pipeline is expected to contribute to 2026 budgets.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $30 million for Q2
Operating expenses up to $83 million from $64 million due to onetime fees
International real estate business was a drag, running about $2 million negative adjusted EBITDA per quarter
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 7% YoY; core segment revenue up 8% and 99% recurring
Core segment like-for-like EBITDA margin improved from 20% to 26%
New client wins and expanded mandates totaling over $900 million projected billable assets in H1
summary: AlTi reported Q2 2025 consolidated revenue of $53 million, up 7% year-over-year, with core Wealth Management and Capital Solutions revenue up 8% to $52 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $4 million consolidated and $14 million in the core segment, with like-for-like core EBITDA margin improving from 20% to 26% excluding a Q1 incentive fee. Management highlighted timing mismatches, including onetime ZBB fees of $7 million and only partial Kontora contribution, with $20 million in annual savings expected from ZBB starting in the second half. The company completed the Kontora acquisition and exited international real estate, aiming to simplify and improve margins.

negative_highlights: Production slower than Q1 due to deliberate activity reduction and completion timing
Second quarter CapEx down 30% sequentially due to dropping a rig in May
Uncertainty around adding second rig in September; retains flexibility to delay
positive_highlights: Generated over $155 million of EBITDAX in Q2 with margins of $33.58 per BOE
Refinanced term loan and RBL, extending maturities to September 2028 and boosting liquidity
Simul-frac on first pad saved ~$400,000 per well, ~10% completion cost reduction
summary: HighPeak Energy reported a solid Q2 2025 with EBITDAX over $155 million and strong margins of $33.58 per BOE, despite lower commodity prices. Production was slightly below Q1 due to planned activity reductions and completion timing, but management reaffirmed full-year 2025 production guidance. The company reduced CapEx by 30% sequentially, dropped to one rig in mid-May, and plans to add a second rig in September, though it retains flexibility to delay. They completed a debt refinancing extending maturities to 2028 and added hedges covering over 50% of H2 volumes at a weighted average floor above $62.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 53% from 67% due to revenue mix
Marketplace revenue soft at $0.3 million due to halted marketing spend
Credit business revenue declined year-over-year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 18% YoY, with fintech up 28% excluding one-time vendor true-up
First-half net loss improved 46% to $12.8 million
Realized $9M of $11M annualized cost savings in H1
summary: Q2 FY2025 net revenue was $7.1 million, up 18% YoY, with Fintech revenue at $3.4 million (up 15.6%, but would have been $3.8 million or 28% without a $0.4 million vendor true-up), Brands/EveryLife at $3.3 million (up 45.5%), and Marketplace soft at $0.3 million. Gross margin declined to 53% from 67% due to mix. GAAP operating loss improved to $8.1 million from $14 million, and net loss per share improved to -$0.18 from -$0.36. Management announced plans to monetize EveryLife and Marketplace to focus entirely on fintech, expecting completion by Q4 2025. First-half OpEx declined 13% and net loss improved 46%, with $9 million of the expected $11 million annualized savings realized in H1.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $2.1 million from $3.6 million
Gearing segment reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.1 million
Guidance suspended due to pending asset sale
positive_highlights: Q2 orders of $21 million, up 14% year-over-year
Industrial Solutions record orders and backlog; third straight quarter of records
Gearing orders up 45% and $6 million follow-on order received in July
summary: Q2 2025 revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $39.2 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.1 million from $3.6 million, with margin down to 5.3% due to capacity inefficiencies. Orders grew 14% to $21 million, with Industrial Solutions setting a record for orders and backlog. The company suspended full-year guidance due to the pending sale of Manitowoc, expecting $13 million cash and $8 million annual cost savings. Gearing continued to rebound with a new $6 million order in July.

negative_highlights: NAUTILUS missed primary effectiveness endpoint in earlier time-to-event analysis
Operating expenses grew 13%, though below sales growth
Executive transition incurred onetime nonrecurring items
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $23.5M, up 22% YoY
Raised full-year revenue and gross margin guidance
NAUTILUS data showing >80% median GTC seizure reduction at 18-24 months and 45.2% seizure-free at 12 months
summary: NeuroPace reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $23.5 million, up 22% year-over-year, with total gross margin above 77% and RNS gross margin above 80%. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $94-$98 million and gross margin to 75%-76%, citing strong RNS System sales and Project CARE expansion. Management highlighted compelling NAUTILUS data for IGE, with median GTC seizure reduction signaling better than 80% at 18 and 24 months and 45.2% seizure-free at 12 months, and reaffirmed PMA supplement submission in H2 2025. They also completed a refinancing and noted positive CMS IPPS outcome preserving current DRG reimbursement.

negative_highlights: Revenue guidance for 2025 maintained at $64-68 million, implying significant back-half weighted performance
Management notes continued lumpiness in Pharma Biocatalysis revenue due to unpredictable order timing
Gross margin improvement to 72% is not expected to be sustained at that magnitude for the full year
positive_highlights: Revenue in Q2 2025 was $15.3 million, nearly double the $8 million reported in Q2 2024
Operating loss halved year-over-year, with net loss improving to $13.3 million from $23.8 million
Customer engagements for ECO Synthesis exceed 30, with growing interest approaching 40
summary: Codexis reported Q2 2025 revenue of $15.3 million, up from $8 million in Q2 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 72% from 45%. Net loss narrowed to $13.3 million from $23.8 million year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $64-68 million, with growth expected in the second half from ligase and ECO Synthesis. They reported over 30 (approaching 40) customer engagements for ECO Synthesis and are exploring options to expand capacity, including a potential Codexis-owned GMP facility to capture more value from early-phase projects.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to hardware mix
Operating loss of $5 million in Q2 2025
SG&A reduction partially offset by higher R&D costs
positive_highlights: Revenue up 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million
Secured major IAM deployment with National Bank of Mozambique
Closed $600,000 follow-on orders from defense ministry, total project over EUR 3 million
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue increased 49% year-over-year to $1.7 million, with hardware revenue up $458,000, but gross margin declined to 73% from 77% due to product mix. SG&A was reduced 13.5% year-over-year, partially offset by higher R&D, and the company reduced its note payable from $1.5 million to $447,000. Management highlighted new defense contracts, including a first phase deployment for an international defense agency, a 3-year PortalGuard deployment with a Middle East police force, and $600,000 of follow-on orders. Despite a $5 million operating loss in Q2, management expects expense run rate to normalize and sees strong growth opportunities in defense and EMEA in the back half of 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margin only 16% in Q2, with fluctuation expected
Cash burn still $7.3 million in quarter; annualized burn remains
ATM program of $75 million launched, indicating financing need
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue up 46% YoY; first-half revenue exceeded all of 2024
Raised NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million
Signed SOW with top-5 OEM; shipping units, targeting 2027 SOP

Cash burn fell to $7.3 million from $20.7 million in Q1, and the company raised its NRE booking guidance to $30-60 million from $20-50 million. Management launched the InnovizSMART non-automotive product and signed a development agreement with a top-5 OEM for a 2027 L3 program, while maintaining full-year revenue guidance of $50-60 million. The company is ramping production at Fabrinet and expects 10x unit shipments in Q3 versus Q2.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss only improved 43% due to continued THP investment
THP strategic alternatives process initiated, limiting ability to communicate
Additional EUR 2 million OsStic milestone payments remain uncertain in timing
positive_highlights: Surgical net revenue up 28% YoY to $25.8 million
Segment adjusted EBITDA up 239% YoY to $4.7 million
THP pilot program initiated and CarePICS acquisition completed
summary: Sanara MedTech's Surgical segment grew net revenue 28% YoY to $25.8 million, with soft tissue up 28% and bone fusion up 25%. The segment achieved about $500,000 net income, a $2.7 million improvement, and adjusted EBITDA rose 239% to $4.7 million. Management initiated a formal strategic alternatives process for THP and guided second-half THP cash investment down to $5.5-$6.5 million. The company remains on track for OsStic launch in Q1 2027 after BMI completed two milestones.

negative_highlights: No Israel Innovation Authority grant received in Q2, versus $180,000 in prior year
FX headwinds from shekel strength noted, not hedged
Guidance kept at 15-18% growth, implying deceleration from Q2's 19.3%
positive_highlights: Revenue up 19.3% YoY to a record $17.7 million
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to nearly 20% of revenue
Cash at record $101.6 million, debt-free
summary: RADCOM reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $17.7 million, up 19.3% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.4 million (19.5% of revenue) and non-GAAP net income of $4.2 million ($0.25 per diluted share). Cash reached a record $101.6 million, with positive operating cash flow of $2.6 million. The company maintained full-year revenue guidance of 15-18% growth and noted progress on NVIDIA and ServiceNow partnerships, with some customers moving to lab deployments.

negative_highlights: Guest value perception declined unexpectedly after March menu launch
Company comp traffic down 2.5% in Q2; July started at -0.9%
Full-year guidance lowered; no longer free cash flow positive in 2025
positive_highlights: Same-store sales improved to +5% average in the last 2 weeks
Owned digital traffic up 2% YoY and rewards check-ins up 4% in Q2
Portfolio closures are removing negative-cash-flow restaurants and boosting nearby sales
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q2 FY2025 total revenue of $126.4 million, down 0.7% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 1.5% but traffic down 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $6 million from $9.2 million, and restaurant contribution margin contracted to 12.8% from 15.5%, pressured by $1.7 million in menu-rollout costs. Management cut full-year guidance to revenue of $487-$495 million and comp sales growth of 2.5%-4%, and no longer expects positive free cash flow in 2025. Recent weekly sales trends improved to +5% following the Duos value launch, but overall results missed internal expectations.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 8.8% from 20.6% sequentially due to mix and tariffs
Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 1.4% from 15% sequentially
Revised FY25 non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $24.4-$26.9M on tariffs and mix
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenue of $18.4M and 135 units delivered
Lowest operating loss since going public at $7.1M
Positive free cash flow of $4.6M, highest in company history
summary: Xos reported record Q2 2025 revenue of $18.4 million on 135 units, up from $5.9 million on 29 units in Q1, and highest quarterly deliveries in history. GAAP gross margin declined to 8.8% from 20.6% last quarter due to product mix and tariffs, but operating loss hit a record low of $7.1 million and free cash flow was positive at $4.6 million. Management reaffirmed FY2025 revenue guidance of $50.2-$65.8 million and unit deliveries of 320-420, but revised non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $24.4-$26.9 million due to mix and tariffs. The convertible note repayment was amended to extend through 2028, and the company highlighted growth in powertrain orders from Blue Bird and increased interest in the MDXT.

negative_highlights: Deal activity constrained due to tariff and regulatory uncertainty

summary: Greenfire announced a transformational recapitalization plan to fully repay senior secured notes via a $300 million equity rights offering backstopped by Waterous Energy Fund and secure an upsized $275 million credit facility, leaving the company debt-free after closing. Production is expected to hit the top end of 2025 guidance of 15,000-16,000 bbl/d, with capital guidance reaffirmed at $130 million. The company approved a $180 million 2026 capital budget with flat production guidance of 15,500-16,500 bpd, due to growth projects not reaching first oil until late Q4 2026 and a planned May 2026 turnaround. The boiler outage was resolved ahead of schedule, but the second boiler is being refurbished, and sulfur removal facilities are expected operational in November 2025.

The company grew checking accounts 23%, grew noninterest-bearing deposits to 16.3% of total deposits, and expects further margin expansion in 2026, targeting a 1% ROA. Management guided to core quarterly expenses of $23-24 million for 2026 and expressed confidence in achieving sustainable 1% ROA.

The company raised $5.38 million via share sales, boosting cash by 89% to CNY 15.9 million, and invested in facility upgrades and headcount recovery (from 68 to 97 employees). Management framed 2025 as a 'transformative' recovery year and reaffirmed a three-stage strategic plan, with stage one (recovery) expected through 2026, but provided no specific forward revenue or earnings guidance.

summary: Aviat Networks reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $111.5 million, down from $118.2 million a year ago, but six-month revenues were $218.8 million, up 5.9% year over year. Gross margins contracted year over year due to mix, but improved sequentially for the first half. Management kept full-year FY2026 guidance unchanged, noted highest Q2 bookings in ten years, and highlighted initial orders for its PISA cellular router and MDU solution, while keeping BEAD out of guidance.

Management announced exits from select Canadian consumer cannabis markets and divestiture of Bevo plant propagation, expecting improved margins and EBITDA thereafter, while also filing a $100 million ATM for strategic purposes. Guidance for fiscal 2026 global medical cannabis revenue was reiterated at $269-$281 million, implying 10-15% growth.

Segment highlights included EV charging revenue nearly doubling to $4.7 million and strong gross margin expansion, while LED lighting revenue declined. Management cited a new $14-15 million exterior lighting project and continued cost discipline as key drivers.

Retail sales in North America were up year-over-year with December accelerating, but international retail especially EMEA was softer. Management sees 2026 as a transition year, expects margins under pressure, and announced at least $150 million of annual run-rate savings impacting 2027 and beyond. Management raised 2026 guidance with written premium growth expected to accelerate to 15%-16%, driven by a new fronting arrangement with Markel that allows retention of 100% of premium and expansion of State Farm Classic+ and Enthusiast Plus products.
