negative_highlights: Net loss of $193 million due to $136 million impairment charges
Adjusted EBITDA down 23% to $284 million on lower Brent prices
Operating expenses up 23% to $249 million, though per BOE down 6%
positive_highlights: Successfully executed bond exchange with ~88% participation, enhancing liquidity
2025 production up 32% to 45,709 boe/d, driven by Ecuador and Canada
Rahoo-2 well producing ~790 bbl/d at <1% water cut, ahead of expectations
summary: Gran Tierra reported a net loss of $193 million in 2025, including $136 million in impairment charges, versus net income of $3.2 million in 2024; adjusted EBITDA fell 23% to $284 million and funds flow from operations declined to $178 million. Production rose 32% to 45,709 boe/d. Management highlighted a successful bond exchange with 88% participation, enhanced liquidity, entry into Azerbaijan, and improved 2026 hedging with an average floor around $60. Despite lower profits, the company is positioned for debt reduction and growth, with shares trading at a meaningful discount to NAV.

negative_highlights: Increased competition in the NAD space, particularly from NMN products.
NOPARK Parkinson's study did not achieve primary endpoint.
Guidance for 2026 is conservative, with back-half-loaded revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 30% YoY, exceeding initial 18% growth guidance.
Q4 revenue up 16% YoY; net income positive for the quarter and full year.
Company ended year with $64.8 million cash and no debt.
summary: Q4 revenue was $33.8 million, up 16% YoY, with net income of $4.1 million; full-year revenue reached $129.4 million, up 30% YoY with net income of $17.4 million. Management highlighted strong full-year growth exceeding initial guidance and the launch of Niagen Plus at-home injection kits in H1 2026. They noted increased competition but also cited recent positive scientific studies and ongoing litigation against the FDA regarding NMN. They provided conservative guidance for 2026, with back-half loaded growth expected, while noting potential upside from new products and marketing campaigns.

negative_highlights: C-BEYOND enrollment number inconsistent (press release says 880+; call says 180+).
Phase III data not yet reported; key readouts remain later in 2026.
Commercial launch assumes stable pricing and payer access; no contracts secured yet.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment for C-BEYOND with over 880 patients; top-line results expected midyear.
Cash position of $301.8 million with runway through 2027 supports both programs.
Market research: physicians would prescribe BEM-RZR to ~50% of patients regardless of cirrhosis status.
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q4 2025 cash and investments of $301.8 million, extending runway through 2027. Enrollment completed for the C-BEYOND Phase III HCV trial (over 880 patients) with top-line results expected midyear, and C-FORWARD enrollment expected midyear with results by year-end. The company initiated IND-enabling studies for AT-587, a first-in-class HEV candidate, and aims for a first-in-human study midyear. Commercial preparation included market research showing physician willingness to prescribe the HCV regimen to ~50% of patients and payer formulary interest.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 10.3% in Q4 and 8.5% for the year on a constant currency basis
Europe/APAC revenue fell 1.4% in Q4 and 2.7% for the year, with continued competitive and rebate pressures
Guidance lowered due to uncertainty from recent Middle East events, particularly potential European demand impact
positive_highlights: North America volume growth of 5.5% in Q4 and 14.3% for the year
Automation revenue grew nearly 40% on a constant currency basis in Q4 and ~35% for the year, exceeding $40 million
Strong liquidity: cash of $63 million and no revolver draws
summary: Ranpak's Q4 2025 revenue grew 2.2% on a constant currency basis, or 4.4% excluding warrants, driven by strong North America e-commerce and automation growth. Adjusted EBITDA declined 10.3% on a constant currency basis, or 1.2% excluding warrants, and full-year EBITDA fell 8.5% (down 2.4% excluding warrants). The company hit the low end of its revised EBITDA guidance but missed the top line slightly due to Europe challenges and automation project delays. Management issued a cautious 2026 outlook, citing Middle East events and potential European demand softness, while expecting automation to turn Adjusted EBITDA positive.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue declined 8% due to contract timing and deferred amortization.
Residential generator market slowed due to high interest rates and fewer outages.
AIO partnership not expected to contribute revenue until second half of 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 4.5% to $11.478 million, a record year.
Monitoring revenue grew 22% with 95% gross margin.
Cash flow from operations more than doubled to $2.09 million, up 131%.
summary: Acorn Energy reported record 2025 revenue of $11.478 million, up 4.5% YoY, with monitoring revenue growing 22% and gross margin improving to 76.8% from 72.8%. Operating cash flow more than doubled to $2.09 million, and the company remains debt-free with $4.45 million in cash. Management reaffirmed a 20% average annual revenue growth target over 3-5 years, though hardware revenue declined due to a large customer contract timing and a decrease in deferred revenue amortization. The new AIO partnership is expected to contribute revenue in the second half of 2026, but no numbers were given.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.2 million in Q4 2025 from $4.9 million a year ago
Gross margin declined to 67% from 71% due to product mix and introductory international pricing
Operating expenses remained elevated at $11.4 million vs $11.3 million prior year
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 43% YoY to $6 million
Commercial inflection point with pipeline of 110 new systems in final sales stages
TULSA reimbursement confirmed for 2026 with Category 1 CPT codes and private payer coverage expected in H2 2026
summary: Profound Medical reported Q4 2025 revenue of $6 million, up 43% year-over-year, with gross margin at 67% versus 71% in Q4 2024 due to product mix and introductory international pricing. The net loss widened to $8.2 million from $4.9 million, with cash at $59.7 million. Management highlighted a growing sales pipeline (110 systems in final sales stages), continued reimbursement momentum with CPT Category 1 codes confirmed for 2026, and early international distribution success in Saudi Arabia and Australia. They reiterated a path to profitable growth, targeting ~$85 million annual revenue with 200 sites and 50 procedures per site, and expect high double-digit to low triple-digit revenue growth in 2026. Upcoming CAPTAIN trial data presentations are key catalysts.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened to $21M from $3M in prior quarter.
Gain on sale margin declined to 324 bps from 339 bps, with Q1 guidance of 270-300 bps.
Cash decreased by $122M from prior quarter to $337M.
positive_highlights: Origination volume of $8.0B was highest since 2022, up 23% from prior quarter.
Recapture rate reached 71% from in-house servicing platform.
Adjusted revenue up 10% YoY with expense growth under 1% for full year.
summary: loanDepot reported Q4 2025 adjusted net loss of $21 million, worse than the $3 million loss in Q3, due to lower gain on sale margin, higher MSR amortization, and higher expenses. Pull-through weighted lock volume rose 4% to $7.3 billion, and origination volume hit $8.0 billion, the highest since 2022 and up 23% sequentially. Gain on sale margin was 324 basis points at the high end of guidance but down from 339 bps. Q1 2026 guidance calls for lock volume of $7.75-8.75 billion and margin of 270-300 bps. Management emphasized market share gains, a 71% recapture rate, and investments in AI and technology to drive operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined 5% to $8.3 million
Ended the year with only $1.2 million in cash despite $7 million raised
Critical care revenue declined 19% for the full year and 24% in the fourth quarter
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 68.2% in Q4, up 9.9 percentage points year-over-year
U.S. console sales increased 208% with eight units sold versus three in prior-year
Heart failure and pediatrics grew 814% year-over-year
summary: Nuwellis reported Q4 2025 revenue of $2.4 million, up 4% year-over-year and 9% sequentially, with gross margin expanding to 68.2% from 58.4%. Full-year revenue declined 5% to $8.3 million, with heart failure and pediatrics growing 814% each, offset by a 19% decline in critical care. The company ended the year with $1.2 million cash and no debt, but raised $7 million and reduced guidance on cash burn. Management is focused on operational restructuring, exiting EU markets, terminating a clinical trial, and integrating a new acquisition to drive future growth.

negative_highlights: Q4 results are quiet and should be viewed in full-year context, indicating lumpy revenue
Expects CHMP to recommend withdrawal of the mpox indication
No new U.S. procurement contract announced; timing uncertain
positive_highlights: Secured $27 million in U.S. government development funding during 2025
Received a $13 million international order from a repeat Asia-Pacific customer
Ended 2025 with $155 million cash and no debt
summary: SIGA reported full-year 2025 product revenues of approximately $88 million, with $53 million from oral TPOXX and $26 million from IV TPOXX under the BARDA 19C contract, plus $6 million international sales. Pretax operating income was about $24 million, net income about $23 million, and diluted EPS $0.32. The company ended 2025 with $155 million cash and no debt, and has $26 million of outstanding U.S. government orders expected to deliver in 2026. Management remains engaged with the U.S. government but gave no timing on a new procurement contract, while the EMA CHMP is expected to issue a context in March, with management expecting the smallpox indication maintained and the mpox indication withdrawn.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $1.9M from $2.1M despite higher revenue, due to supply disruption and underutilization
Gearing segment reported adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.3M, revenue down 8% YoY
Supply disruption in Heavy Fab reduced throughput and operating efficiency; Gearing capacity utilization lower
positive_highlights: Industrial Solutions revenue up 60% YoY, highest ever recorded; segment EBITDA margin expanded to 16% (vs 10% prior year)
Backlog in Industrial Solutions hit new record of $38M, fifth consecutive record quarter; Gearing backlog at highest since 2023 ($26M)
Received $6.0M follow-on order for natural gas turbine gearing in March, adding to Q1 orders of ~$11M
summary: Broadwind reported Q4 2025 revenue of $37.7 million, up 12% year-over-year, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.9 million from $2.1 million due to a raw material supply disruption and lower Gearing utilization. Industrial Solutions revenue jumped 60% to a record $9.4 million, and backlog hit a new record of $38 million. Gearing orders rose 38% to $9.7 million, with total backlog reaching $26 million, and the company reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $140-150 million revenue and $8-10 million adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Ex-political growth of 28% in Q4 but guide implies slowdown to high teens in Q1
Full-year performance absorbed tariff pressure and client migration
Q1 guidance slowed due to seasonality and advertiser mix
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 22% YoY, above the high end of quarterly guidance
CTV contribution ex-TAC grew over 40% for the second consecutive year
New flagship customers Molson Coors and WHOOP live and ramping
summary: Viant Technology reported Q4 FY2025 revenue up 22% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 19%, both above the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $24.7 million, also exceeding guidance. Full-year 2025 revenue increased 19% to $344 million, with contribution ex-TAC up 18%. Management highlighted accelerating CTV growth (46% of spend), strong new customer wins (Molson Coors, WHOOP), and the launch of their AI-driven Outcomes product, while acknowledging Q1 2026 growth is expected to moderate to high teens due to seasonality and advertiser mix.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 included a one-time restructuring charge.
ECO business currently services-based with limited gross margin contribution.
Guidance includes a speculative portion per CFO comments.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 19% YoY to $70.4 million; gross margin expanded to 64%.
Signed three CDMO agreements and first commercial contract for ECOsynthesis siRNA.
Raised 2026 revenue guidance to $72-76 million.
summary: Codexis reported full-year 2025 revenue of $70.4 million, up from $59.3 million in 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 64% from 56%. The company signed three CDMO agreements with Bachem, Nitto Avecia, and Axolabs, and announced its first contract for fully enzymatic siRNA supply (low 7-figure) with an emerging biotech. Management provided 2026 revenue guidance of $72-76 million and expects current cash to fund operations through 2027. A one-time restructuring charge was taken in Q4, and the company expects to sign another licensing-type deal in 2026.

negative_highlights: Suspended dividend to save $20-25 million annually, reflecting market not crediting the payout
Northeast Flat Top area has six wells with anomalous water inflows; no new drilling there in 2026
High cost of capital (10%+ interest) on term loan, with debt reduction as a priority
positive_highlights: Quarter-to-date 2026 production averaging over 46,000 BOE/d, roughly 10% above the midpoint of guidance
Capital budget ~50% lower than 2025, with estimated 65% increase in production per dollar invested
More than 2,600 total drilling locations across stacked formations, with over 100 rig-years of inventory
summary: HighPeak Energy's Q4 2025 earnings release focuses on a conservative 2026 plan prioritizing balance sheet strength and free cash flow over production growth. The company has suspended its dividend (saving $20-25 million annually) and reduced its 2026 capital budget by nearly 50% year-over-year, with early 2026 production of over 46,000 BOE/d running about 10% above the midpoint of guidance. Management has expanded hedging and plans to pay down debt aggressively, especially with stronger oil prices, but also highlights six wells with anomalous water inflows in the Northeast Flat Top area, leading to no new drilling there in 2026.

negative_highlights: 2026 guidance tempered by M&T's double-digit revenue decline due to prior bookings lag
PathFactory acquisition adds investment costs and integration uncertainty for 2026
FX headwinds from Israeli shekel continue to pressure expectations
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3M, tenth consecutive quarter of profitability
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA grew 150% YoY, above original guidance
PathFactory acquisition adds AI-driven content journey orchestration, with run rate in teens of millions
summary: Kaltura reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $45.5 million and subscription revenue of $42.7 million, with record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of profitability. Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $18.6 million, up 150% year-over-year and above original guidance. The company announced the planned acquisition of PathFactory for about $22 million, expanding its agentic digital experience platform, and guided 2026 with caution, citing headwinds from M&T revenue decline and PathFactory's contribution timing. New product launches include agentic avatars and an Avatar SDK, with revenue expected in the second half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Fintech non-GAAP gross margin fell from 96% to 69% due to mix shift
Operating loss of $32 million for 2025, though improved by $9.7 million
Cash and restricted cash only $16.1 million with $6.2 million drawn on credit line
positive_highlights: 2025 net revenue of $18.2 million exceeded guidance of $16.5 million, up 81% YoY
Q4 fintech revenue up 109% YoY and 100%+ QoQ
G&A expenses reduced by $9.9 million (26%) YoY
summary: PSQH reported 2025 net revenue from continuing operations of $18.2 million, an 81% increase year-over-year and above guidance of $16.5 million. Q4 fintech revenue grew 109% to $7.3 million, with credit revenue up 47% to $4.8 million. The company reduced operating loss by $9.7 million versus prior year, cut headcount by over 40%, and expects annualized cash savings of about $8 million. Management is focused on fintech-only strategy, with divestitures of brand and marketplace underway.

negative_highlights: Q4 total revenue growth of 5% was softer than prior-year's hurricane-boosted quarter
THP wind-down required $5.3M cash use in H2 2025
OsStic U.S. launch not until Q1 2027, no near-term revenue contribution
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue at high end of guidance, up 13% ex hurricane BIASURGE
Gross margin up ~200 bps to 93%, adjusted EBITDA up 86% to $17M
Vizient Innovative Technology contract for BIASURGE expands access to ~1,800 facilities
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $27.5 million, up 5% YoY, or 13% excluding $1.8 million of hurricane-related BIASURGE sales, at the high end of guidance. Full-year revenue reached $103.1 million, up 19%, with gross margin expansion to 93% (up 200 bps) and adjusted EBITDA up 86% to $17 million. The company reaffirmed 2026 net revenue growth guidance of 13%–17% and highlighted a new Vizient Innovative Technology contract for BIASURGE, effective January 1, 2026, providing access to ~1,800 facilities.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $6.8 million in Q4, though improved from $9.7 million last year
Fourth quarter total revenue only up 0.8% due to store closures
Company closed 33 restaurants in 2025 and expects 30-35 more in 2026
positive_highlights: System-wide comp sales up 6.6% in Q4, accelerating to over 9% in Q1 2026
Adjusted EBITDA up over 88% in Q4, with 2026 guidance more than doubling prior year
Restaurant contribution margin expanded 290 basis points to 14.1% in 2025
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $122.8 million, up 0.8% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 6.6%. Restaurant contribution margin expanded to 14.1% from 11.2%, and adjusted EBITDA rose over 88% to $7.6 million. The company guided 2026 to comp sales of 6-9% and adjusted EBITDA of $30-35 million, more than double prior year, with early Q1 2026 comp trends over 9%. Management attributes momentum to portfolio optimization, menu innovation, and operational improvements.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue of $5.2 million was seasonally light and down sharply from Q2's $18.4 million
Large fleet agreements may compress near-term margins
No formal 2026 revenue or EPS guidance provided
positive_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue reached $46 million on 328 units, the highest ever
Generated $5.4 million positive free cash flow versus negative $49.1 million in 2024
Accounts receivable reduced to $6 million from $26.9 million, including $9.9 million UPS collection
summary: Xos reported Q4 2025 revenue of $5.2 million on 34 units delivered, with the balance of a 200+ unit UPS program recognized in future periods. Full-year 2025 revenue was $46 million on 328 units, up from prior years, with GAAP gross margin of 5.9%, operating loss narrowed 28% to $33.1 million, and positive free cash flow of $5.4 million versus negative $49.1 million in 2024. The company ended the year with $14 million in cash, down $26.9 million to $6 million in accounts receivable, and renegotiated its convertible note with Aldermay to quarterly installments through 2028. Management guided to expanding operations in 2026 with an upgraded hub product in three configurations, a growing powertrain business with Blue Bird, and continued focus on working capital and inventory turns, while being selective on ATM usage.

negative_highlights: Market cap at discount to treasury valuation
Crypto sector out of favor, impacting digital treasury companies
Earlier stage biotech funding scarce
positive_highlights: Net income of $1.23 billion and EPS of $25.48 for 2025
FDA clearance for Phase IIb knee osteoarthritis trial
Extended RAIN token option to Dec 31, 2027 at same price
summary: For full-year 2025, Enlivex reported net income of $1.23 billion and diluted EPS of $25.48, driven by appreciation in treasury assets tied to the Rain Protocol prediction markets token. The company entered a $21 million convertible debt financing, extended its Rain token option to 2027, and approved a $20 million buyback. Clinically, FDA cleared a Phase IIb trial in knee osteoarthritis, with top-line data expected in 2027.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $155 million for the year.
CEO transition and ongoing strategic review add uncertainty.
Operating leverage not yet visible due to onetime costs.
positive_highlights: Total revenues up 29% year-over-year to $255 million.
Management fees grew 9% to nearly $200 million; Q4 management fees up 14% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $35 million for the year.
summary: AlTi reported full-year 2025 total revenues of $255 million, up 29% year-over-year, with management fees near $200 million, up 9%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $35 million, but the company posted a GAAP net loss of $155 million, including a $35 million impairment in Q3. AUM reached $50 billion, up 10% year-over-year, aided by the Kontora acquisition. CEO Michael Tiedemann is stepping down, with Nancy Curtin as Interim CEO; a special committee continues evaluating strategic alternatives, and Allianz has filed a 13D. Management expects 2026 to show clearer operating leverage from zero-based budgeting and simplified operations.

negative_highlights: FY2025 revenue fell 12% to $6.1M
Gross margin declined to 77.5% from 81.4%
Net loss widened to $4.6M from $4.3M
positive_highlights: Q1 2026 revenue guided to $2.2M, up 37% YoY with better bottom-line improvement
Foreign bank renewed at over $1M for 2026, a ~30% increase
Cash up $2M+ to $2.7M and book value doubled to $7.6M
summary: BIO-key reported FY2025 revenue of $6.1 million, down 12% YoY, with hardware revenue more than doubling to $1.3 million and services up 6%. Net loss widened to $4.6 million but per-share improved to $0.69. Management guides Q1 2026 revenue to about $2.2 million, up 37% YoY, and expects to approach breakeven in early 2026. Key drivers include an expanded $1M+ renewal from a foreign bank, EMEA transition to branded solutions, and new product launches like EcoID III and PortalGuard 7.0.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents only $1.1 million at year-end
Revenue remains lumpy and company does not provide 2026 guidance
Operating expenses reduction driven partly by severance and fundamental shift away from R&D
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 133% YoY; full-year revenue up 40% to $1.7 million
First order for Nu.Q Cancer clinical certification; Nu.Q NETs inclusion in French government-backed $7.3 million DETECSEPS sepsis program
Two licensing agreements signed (Werfen and Hologic); $5 million feline milestone expected this year
summary: For full fiscal year 2025, VolitionRX reported $1.7 million in revenue, up 40% year-over-year, with Q4 revenue growing 133% year-over-year. Operating expenses decreased 17% to $4.8 million lower than 2024, and net cash used in operating activities fell 24% to $19.7 million. Cash at year-end was $1.1 million, but subsequent to year-end the company raised $5.4 million via ATM and $1.9 million via convertible note, plus received $2.3 million in non-dilutive funding. Management expects to collect a $5 million milestone payment from the feline cancer study and plans to cut cash operating expenses by another 25-30% during 2026. First commercial orders for Nu.Q Cancer and Nu.Q NETs were received, and licensing discussions with about 10 companies are ongoing.

negative_highlights: Total revenue up only 0.3% YoY, below 4-8% guidance pace
Jafra Mexico revenue moderated due to productivity focus, associate base declined
Q1 had one fewer week, impacting reported growth; Betterware comparable growth 3.3%
positive_highlights: EBITDA grew 14% YoY, margin expanded 211 bps to 17.4%
Jafra US net revenue up 8.6% in USD, associate base up 3.4%
Tupperware transaction expected Q2 approval, immediately accretive ~40% to EPS
summary: BeFra reported flat revenue growth of 0.3% YoY, below the high end of its 4-8% full-year guidance, but delivered a 14% EBITDA increase with margin expanding 211 bps to 17.4% (18.4% ex-Tupperware expenses). Management highlighted improving associate trends at Betterware, strong Jafra US growth of 8.6% in USD, and the expected Q2 approval of the accretive Tupperware acquisition, which will add ~40% to EPS. They maintained full-year revenue growth guidance of 4-8%, with an expected inflection in Jafra Mexico starting in Q2.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined to $3.4 million from $3.8 million
Advertising revenue slowed late Q1 due to geopolitical issues
EPS reduced by $0.13 due to member acquisition costs
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 5% year-over-year, with growth across all segments
Club member growth up 112% year-over-year
Expect membership fees to account for over 20% of revenue this year
summary: Q1 2026 revenue rose 5% YoY to $24.3 million, but operating profit fell to $3.4 million (14% of revenue) from $3.8 million, partly due to higher marketing spend on club member acquisition. The company guided for continued revenue growth and expects margins to recover as renewals grow, but noted a slowdown in advertising revenue late in Q1 due to the war and geopolitical uncertainty. Membership fees are expected to exceed 20% of revenue this year.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS declined to $0.30 from $0.92 YoY due to prior-year gain on deconsolidation
Mortgage revenue impacted by market volatility late in Q1, masking an otherwise blowout quarter
positive_highlights: Operating EPS up 126% YoY to $0.33, ROA doubled to 84 bps
Net interest margin expanded to 3.43% from 3.15% YoY, with expectations for further expansion
Revenue up ~34% YoY with only 4% OpEx growth, showing strong operating leverage
summary: Primis Financial reported Q1 FY2026 operating EPS of $0.33, up 126% from $0.14 in the year-ago quarter, with ROA improving to 84 bps from 40 bps. NIM expanded to 3.43% from 3.15%, and loans grew 11.7% YoY to $3.4B, with mortgage warehouse near $460M. Management highlighted strong operating leverage (revenue up 34%, OpEx up only 4%) and raised its mortgage production outlook to ~$1.8B for 2026, while guiding to further margin expansion and an aspirational 1% ROA by year-end.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down 470 basis points to 36.5% due to higher tariffs
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.24 from $0.73 in the prior year
Georgia Boot saw slight single-digit decline, though timing-driven
positive_highlights: Q1 sales up 9.1% year-over-year to $124.4 million, in line with expectations
Retail sales increased 16.5% to $42.7 million
Best booking season ever noted across new spring and fall 2026 products
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q1 FY2026 sales of $124.4 million, up 9.1% year-over-year, in line with expectations. Gross margin fell 470 basis points to 36.5% due to over $7 million in higher tariffs, and adjusted EPS dropped to $0.24 from $0.73. The company reiterated full-year guidance of ~6% revenue growth, with tariffs expected to be a ~$10 million headwind split roughly 70/30 between Q1 and Q2. Management cited strong full-price watching, D2C growth, and improving wholesale trends, but noted tariff uncertainty ahead.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 4.3% ex-divestiture, driven by lower print and agency volumes
Agency solution sales pulled back and project work shifting to AOR engagements
USPS rate increase expected up to 10% for Co-mail clients; European divestiture note payment past due
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS up 25% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 7.2% to 7.7%
Returned $7 million to shareholders including dividend increase of 33%
summary: Quad reported Q1 2026 net sales of $581 million, down 4.3% excluding the European divestiture, with adjusted EBITDA of $45 million versus $46 million a year ago and adjusted diluted EPS up 25% to $0.25. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 7.7% from 7.2% due to cost actions and productivity. Management maintained full-year guidance despite postage increases and a temporary ink surcharge, while noting free cash flow was negative $107 million in the quarter, and a $6 million payment from the European divestiture was past due.

negative_highlights: Fraud charge-off of $0.22 per share hit earnings
Net interest margin compressed due to rate cuts and high deposit costs
At-risk non-performing loans increased to $13.2M
positive_highlights: Loan originations up 56% YoY, 65% QoQ
SBA gain on sale margin 4.79% exceeded budget of 4%
April SBA sales already at $39.5M with $2M gain
summary: GBank reported Q1 FY2026 results impacted by a $0.22 per share charge-off related to third-party credit card fraud, which management attributes to bot attacks on a canceled retail card program. Despite this, loan originations surged 56% YoY to $208 million, surpassing $1 billion in on-balance-sheet loans, and SBA gain on sale margins reached 4.79% versus a 4% budget. Net interest margin compressed due to rate cuts and high deposit costs, but management expects improvement in Q2. The company continues to develop its gaming fintech platforms, including Bold Bets V2 and a new Bankroll joint venture.

negative_highlights: Adjusted sales down 7.3% YoY to $83.9 million
Elektron sales declined 14.8% due to lower volumes and timing
Cash from operations was an outflow of $4.1 million in the quarter
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 17% YoY to $0.27, ahead of expectations
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 220 bps to 14.7% despite lower sales
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to a midpoint of $1.17
summary: Luxfer reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.27, up 17% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 8.8% to $12.3 million and EBITDA margin up 220 basis points to 14.7%, despite sales down 7.3% to $83.9 million. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to a midpoint of $1.17, from a range of $1.12-$1.22, citing improved visibility and a strong start to the year. Management also outlined a credible path to robust double-digit earnings growth in 2027, driven by SCBA replacement, aerospace and defense strength, and operational initiatives.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9% year-over-year, with U.S. down 7% and international down 12% (down 21% constant currency).
International revenue decline fully attributed to the absence of China distributor sales; Chinese registration renewal expected only in second half 2026.
Revenue guidance implies no meaningful China contribution in the back half, and return to growth is back-half loaded.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 78% from 73% year-over-year, driven by lower distributor mix.
Excluding China, international revenue grew 22% year-over-year, up 9% constant currency.

The company is on track for a phase III readout in Q3 2027 and plans a rolling NDA submission starting Q1 2027. Long-term OLE data show durable seizure control and statistically significant improvements in cognition and behavior through four years, with a strong safety profile. The company has a pro forma cash position of approximately $420 million, providing runway to a potential U.S. launch by early 2028. Additionally, STK-002 for ADOA has completed dosing of the first cohort and is advancing to higher doses, with early results expected in the first half of 2027.

Management highlighted strong growth in launched and acquired products (18% operational, 27% excluding one-time items), particularly from legacy Seagen (21% US growth ex-items), and increased net cost savings expectations to $6.7 billion through 2029. summary: Q2 2026 marked the first full quarter of the U.S. launch of IMCIVREE for acquired hypothalamic obesity, with strong early demand: over 400 start forms from ~300 unique prescribers in 14 weeks, and positive payer access. Management highlighted encouraging RM-718 phase II data showing 11.6% mean BMI reduction at 16 weeks, comparable to setmelanotide and bivamelagon, with no generalized hyperpigmentation. The company reaffirmed its long-term conviction in HO and plans to initiate the bivamelagon phase III trial in HO by end of 2026. No specific financial figures were disclosed in the provided text.

Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded ~240 bps to 23.3%
Onsite Health Clinics organic revenue grew 27.9% YoY
summary: Concentra reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $606 million, up 10% YoY, with core revenue up 8% excluding acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA grew 22.5% to $140.9 million, with margin expansion of ~240 bps to 23.3%. Adjusted EPS increased ~40% to $0.52. Management raised or reiterated guidance, noted strong organic growth in Onsite Health Clinics, and announced a CEO succession. Leverage fell below 3x, and the company continued buybacks and dividends.

positive_highlights: Q2 adjusted EBITDA up 30%+ YoY to ~$1.767B
Fleet commercial availability exceeded 97% during July heat waves
Announced Helix digital infrastructure partnership with KKR, NVIDIA, and KIA
summary: Vistra reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.767 billion, up over 30% year-over-year from $1.35 billion, driven by generation gains from higher realized prices, PJM capacity revenues, and retail contributions. The company reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8-$7.6 billion and expects to deliver at or above the midpoint. Management announced a founding investment of up to $1 billion in Helix Digital Infrastructure with KKR, NVIDIA, and KIA, and maintained its 2027 EBITDA opportunity range despite lower ERCOT forward curves.

Record backlog and raised fiscal 2026 guidance for 30%+ growth on revenue and bottom-line margins
Completed strategic acquisition of Ellsworth Construction in Oklahoma, expanding data center exposure
summary: Construction Partners reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with revenue of $999.4 million, up 28.2% year-over-year (8.9% organic, 19.3% acquisitive), adjusted EBITDA of $163 million (up 24%), and adjusted EPS of $1.08. The company raised its fiscal 2026 guidance to reflect over 30% growth in both revenue and bottom-line margins, and highlighted a record backlog. Management expressed confidence in the federal funding outlook and expects strong organic growth in fiscal 2027, with $140 million of acquisitive revenue carrying over.

positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income exceeded our outlook

summary: Under Armour reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.1 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with North America down 9% and APAC down 7% (or 10% constant currency), while EMEA grew 12% and Latin America grew 8%. Adjusted operating income exceeded expectations despite the revenue miss. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook as consumer demand softened from late May, especially in North America and Asia Pacific, but maintained adjusted operating income guidance. The company continues its SKU reduction strategy and plans to reduce marketing as a percentage of revenue to improve efficiency.

positive_highlights: Net investment income increased to $18.2 million from $10.6 million in Q1
Weighted average risk rating improved to 2.34 from 2.67 in Q1
94% of portfolio rated 3 or better with 54% of companies cash flow positive
summary: Runway Growth Finance reported Q2 2026 total investment income of $37.0 million and net investment income of $18.2 million, up from $29.5 million and $10.6 million in Q1 2026. Total investment portfolio fair value increased 35% to $1.2 billion following the SWK acquisition. Management emphasized portfolio diversification, improved risk ratings (weighted average risk rating down to 2.34 from 2.67), and strong credit quality, highlighting a 76% historical recovery rate. They expressed confidence in the portfolio's fundamentals and repurchase plans despite a disconnect from market pricing.

U.S. customer satisfaction scores improved
summary: Wendy's Q2 FY2026 global systemwide sales declined 6.5%, with U.S. same-restaurant sales down 7.0% and traffic down 12.5%, partially offset by a 5.6% average check increase. The company withdrew its full-year outlook and reduced its dividend. Management acknowledged quality degradation, weakened value proposition, inconsistent operations, and ineffective marketing, outlining five strategic focus areas but providing no specific turnaround details until next quarter.

positive_highlights: Net sales up 7.7%, organic +6.6%, all three businesses grew
Adjusted EBITDA excluding tariff refunds up 27.5%
Home & Garden delivered record quarterly sales of $225 million, above COVID peak
summary: Spectrum Brands reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 7.7% (organic +6.6%), with all three business units growing and Home & Garden setting a record. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.5% excluding tariff refunds, and adjusted EPS was $2.79 including a $1.90 refund benefit. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to mid-single-digit growth excluding refunds, while maintaining flat-to-low-single-digit net sales guidance. The company ended the quarter with $258.9 million cash and net leverage of ~1x, and repurchased ~200,000 shares for $15.8 million.

positive_highlights: Total company sales increased 5% versus prior year quarter
Operating income up $11 million year-over-year
Year-to-date net sales up 15% and profit before income taxes turned from loss to $32.2 million
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported Q3 FY2026 net sales up 5% year-over-year, with operating income of $18.3 million, up $11 million, aided by a one-time $15 million tariff refund. Gross margin improved to 45.3% but would have been modestly lower ex-refunds due to higher raw material costs. The fishing and diving businesses performed well, while camping and watercraft faced weak market conditions. Management noted no additional meaningful tariff refunds expected and cited cost pressures, though year-to-date profitability improved significantly from a prior-year loss.

summary: MSC Income Fund reported Q2 FY2026 ANII of $0.33 per share ($0.36 before taxes) and an annualized ROE of 15.9%. NAV per share rose 4% to $16.51, aided by a realized gain of over $11 million from the exit of Centre Technologies. Private loan investments increased net by $10 million to $848 million fair value in 81 companies, with a weighted average yield of 10.4%. Dividends for Q4 total $0.36 per share, and a new $20 million share repurchase plan plus $20 million from Main Street was authorized.

positive_highlights: RevPAR up nearly 7% ex-Royal Palm, with June growth over 11%
Adjusted EBITDA up nearly 9% to $204 million, margin up 80 bps
Full-year guidance raised across RevPAR, EBITDA, and adjusted FFO per share
summary: Park Hotels & Resorts reported Q2 2026 results that exceeded expectations, with total portfolio RevPAR up nearly 6% to $217 and ex-Royal Palm up nearly 7%. Adjusted EBITDA increased nearly 9% to $204 million, margins expanded 80 bps, and adjusted FFO per share was $0.70. Group revenue grew 9.5% and leisure transient grew over 13%, with strong performance in Hawaii, Florida, and urban markets. The company raised its full-year guidance, with RevPAR now expected at $225, EBITDA at $735 million, and adjusted FFO per share at $2.58-$2.66.

positive_highlights: Revenue up 34% YoY in Q2 and 33% YoY H1, exceeding expectations
Raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoints
Book-to-bill of 1.6x and multiple large contract awards (Telesat, CSA, BAE, Mitsubishi)
summary: MDA Space reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 34% year-over-year to CAD 963 million for the first half, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 187 million and a 19.4% margin. The company raised its full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoints to CAD 1.85 billion and CAD 350 million, respectively. Book-to-bill was 1.6 times in Q2, and major contract expansions included Telesat Lightspeed (225 satellites, +CAD 474 million), a CSA RADARSAT follow-on (over CAD 600 million), and new defense awards. Two acquisitions (Blue Canyon Technologies and CLS) are expected to close in Q4 2026 and Q4 2026-Q1 2027, respectively, with CLS doubling the recurring revenue base.

summary: Gray Media reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $839 million, beating the high end of adjusted guidance by about $9 million with 9% YoY growth. Political revenue surged to $83 million, well above the $60-70 million guidance range. Core advertising was down 1%, better than the mid-single-digit decline guided. The company raised Q3 political guidance to $165-185 million and expects strong Q3/Q4 with political cash flows used for debt reduction. Leverage improved to 5.73x total net leverage, and the board authorized up to $250 million for debt repurchases.
